●  TaskForce Desktop, free and open source

TaskForce is moving to your desktop.

Plan your projects, track your issues and keep what you know in one app, on your own computer. When an issue needs a hand, give it to Claude Code.

Download for Windows

Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit. Also for Linux; macOS is coming.

Hi Alex,

You were one of the first people to use TaskForce, so you are the first to hear it: TaskForce is now a desktop app. Same account, same interface, and your work lives on your own computer. It is free, and its code is open.

A closer look

Plan it, hand it over, keep what you learn.

Plan on a boardProjects, issues, cycles, a roadmap and a backlog. Hand it to Claude CodePick Claude Code as the assignee; it works on your computer and reports back. Keep it in the Brain OSPages linked to each other and to your projects.

Made for the work you do every day.

One place for the work. Your projects, their issues, cycles and pages, and a dashboard with your queue and what changed recently.
Help when you want it. Claude Code takes an issue on your computer and opens a pull request when the project has a GitHub repository. The assistant runs on a local model through Ollama, or on your own API key.
Yours. Your projects stay on your computer, the app sends no usage data, and it keeps working offline once you have signed in.

On Windows

Installed in three steps.

1 DownloadGet the Windows installer from the download page: TaskForce-Setup-1.2.1.exe today, about 270 MB.
2 InstallOpen it: it installs for your account, without administrator rights, then opens TaskForce. After that, updates download by themselves and install when you restart it.
3 Sign inTaskForce opens your browser: sign in with your usual account, by email, Google or GitHub, or create a free one. Then you are in.
If Windows hesitates. The installer is not code-signed yet (a certificate is a paid subscription this free project does not take), so Windows or your antivirus may stop it the first time. Each file is scanned by dozens of antivirus engines first: see the VirusTotal report. The install guide explains each message, SmartScreen, Smart App Control and quarantine, so you decide knowing what it is.

Your work

Bring it along, or start fresh.

I already use TaskForce

Sign in with the same account. In the app, open Operations, click From the web app, then Copy everything.

Each workspace arrives with its Brain OS and its projects: issues, comments, history, cycles, pages and attachments.

It is a copy: the web app keeps your work until it closes. The date is not set yet, and you will get an email before.

To redo by hand: teammates (the app is for one person), GitHub and your other connections, and your AI settings.

Moving from the web app
I'm starting fresh

Install, sign in or create your free account, and go through a three-step setup. TaskForce opens on your own workspace: create a project and add your first issues.

Want Claude Code to pick up issues? Connect it in one click in Settings, Agents. It needs Claude Code installed and signed in with your own account.

Changed your mind later? A whole workspace goes back to the web app from Settings, General, while it is open.

Open source

Built in the open.

The whole of TaskForce is public under the AGPL-3.0 license. You don't need to write code to help: a two-line email is useful too.
